findings.title: #846's headline invariant has an uncovered route: TRUNCATE of the high-water relation re-opens the delete-then-insert hole
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "A version once published for a pair can never be undercut by ANY ROUTE, while retiring a row stays possible." 0244 §B.3 makes the same argument in its own words: "An INSERT wall that reads a relation anybody may delete from is a wall with a door beside it: delete the mark, re-insert low, and the registry is back where #846 found it." But the append-only wall clara._tf_document_capability_high_water_monotone is a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE **FOR EACH ROW** trigger (0244:319-321), and TRUNCATE fires no row triggers. Measured on clara_l03 inside a rolled-back transaction: `truncate clara.document_capability_version_high_water` succeeded (240 marks -> 0), then deleting pdf x invoice (published registry_version 3) and re-inserting it at 2 was ACCEPTED and the table read 2 — #846's own reproducer, verbatim. The estate already owns the mechanism: clara._tf_no_truncate() exists on this database and is installed as a `before truncate ... for each statement` trigger on every other append-only relation (0003_books_core.sql:492-497 for audit_log / journal_entries / journal_lines; 0005_event_spine.sql:282-321 for domain_events, taxonomy_versions, wake_intents, relay_dead_letters). Neither clara.document_capability_version_high_water nor clara.document_capabilities carries one — pg_trigger on both lists only the four #846 triggers plus 0207's.
findings.required_fix: In a follow-up migration (0244 is applied and must not be edited), attach the estate's existing clara._tf_no_truncate() as a BEFORE TRUNCATE FOR EACH STATEMENT trigger on clara.document_capability_version_high_water, with a tail assertion that TRUNCATE is refused and a cell in document-capability-high-water.test.mjs that proves it. If the owner-only threat model is judged acceptable instead, the gap must be written into the ticket and 0244's successor notes rather than left implicit.

findings.title: "planned" wording for line items still stands in the registry's own live column documentation
findings.evidence: Ticket line (AC2): "no 'planned' or 'coming' wording for line items remains in the registry seed, the web copy or the PRD." 0245 changes only the 28 rows' `limits` data; it issues no `comment on column`. Measured on clara_l03 after 0245 and 0246: col_description(clara.document_capabilities.limits) still reads "`{\"invoice_line_items\":\"planned\"}` records the ONE capability deferred by this slice: invoice header facts are persisted with regions today, per-LINE facts are an accepted target with no table yet" (0191:236's text, still live in the catalog). That is the registry's own machine-readable documentation of the very key the ticket re-seeded, still describing line items as a deferred target. The house fix is demonstrated by this lane's own next ticket: 0246 re-issues `comment on column ... business_operation` from the new migration without editing 0191 (0246:202-203).
findings.required_fix: A follow-up migration re-issues `comment on column clara.document_capabilities.limits` describing the accepted-limitation shape (invoice_line_items + invoice_line_items_reason), with a tail assertion that the comment no longer calls line items planned. 0191 and 0245 stay unedited.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md still lists invoice line items as an accepted target marked 'planned' in the capability registry
findings.evidence: Owner ruling on #782 (2026-09-18): "no invoice line items this round; stop promising them"; AC2 asks that the planned/coming wording stop. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:529, a row in the accepted-targets table, still reads `| 发票行项目（line items）的类型化事实 | 能力目录中显式标为 planned，当前不抽取行项目 |`. After 0245 that sentence is factually false about the registry (which now publishes accepted_limitation with a reason), and the row still presents line items as a target Clara intends to build. The AC's named surfaces are the registry seed, the web copy and the PRD — ARCHITECTURE is not named, and work-order rule 5 forbids a lane worker editing docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — so the lane correctly declined and filed it as a follow-up in wave2-lane03-ticket782.md. Confirmed separately: docs/PRD.md has zero 'line item' hits, so the PRD half of the AC really is already satisfied.
findings.required_fix: Orchestrator or a wayfinder pass overwrites that ARCHITECTURE.md row so the accepted target becomes a recorded permanent boundary, per AGENTS.md working-protocol rule 4. Not a lane fix.

findings.title: operationVerdict() branches on business_operation and does not treat proposal_only as distinct from the store-only level
findings.evidence: Ticket line (AC4): "Every reader that renders or branches on `business_operation`, including the Documents workbench, treats the new level as distinct from the store-only level." apps/web/lib/documents/document-state.ts:227-235 `operationVerdict()` reads state.operation.capability — the pair's business_operation level (DocumentStateResult.operation.capability: CapabilityLevel, :125-127) — and branches only on "unsupported" -> not_applicable; supported, stored_only, planned and now proposal_only all fall through to the same entries/statements ladder, so a proposal_only document reads exactly as a stored_only one there, which is the 'undersells what happens' the ticket exists to fix. The rendering surfaces ARE distinct (capability-registry.ts tierStateKey / TIER_STATE_KEYS, capability-tiers.tsx TONE gains proposal_only: text-info with --color-info defined at globals.css:105, en.json capabilityTier.proposal_only = "Proposed, needs confirmation"), and the Documents workbench reaches them through CapabilityTiers (documents-workbench.tsx:282,316 -> UploadPanel / IntakeReceipts). The omission is deliberate and recorded in wave2-lane03-ticket988.md under 'A judgement call', arguing the function never distinguishes any level pair pre-posting; zero rows carry the level today, so nothing is currently mis-rendered.
findings.required_fix: Either accept the recorded judgement call explicitly at integration — the AC is then partial by decision, not omission — or file the follow-up the report itself names: an OperationVerdict value for 'a proposal awaiting a person's confirmation', landing with the first pairing actually classified at the level.

findings.title: "a statement-level constraint trigger" was delivered as a deferred AFTER ROW constraint trigger
findings.evidence: Ticket line (Key interfaces): "clara.document_capabilities: gains the INSERT-side wall and a statement-level constraint trigger." 0244 §B.4 installs `create constraint trigger t_document_capabilities_version_uniform after insert or update or delete ... deferrable initially deferred for each row`, and the file's header records why: `create constraint trigger ... for each statement` is a 42601 syntax error in PostgreSQL (the grammar hard-codes FOR EACH ROW), so the brief's real requirement — a whole-table check at the END of the transaction — is met by the deferral. Verified behaviourally on re-run: document-capability-high-water.test.mjs's third cell refuses a real COMMIT with CLR08 / detail.reason = registry_version_uniform and re-reads the registry unchanged. Recorded so the integrator does not read 'statement-level' in the ticket against 'FOR EACH ROW' in the catalog as a mismatch.
findings.required_fix: None. Keep the header's justification with the file.

findings.title: The user-visible limitation sentence interpolates raw machine tokens
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "every user-visible sentence built from that limit (the document detail, the reading-status copy, en and zh) says the same." The rendered detail now reads "Per-line invoice facts: accepted_limitation. Clara records the header totals with their source regions; ..." and "Reason: no_consumer_reads_line_facts." (en.json:2847-2848; document-state-panel.tsx:328 interpolates the raw limit value into capabilityLimit.*). Before the change the same sentence read '...are planned', which happened to be English. This is not a regression against house shape: the pre-existing OFX limits already render the same way (0191:375 seeds opening_balance = absent_in_format and reader = parse_succeeds_corroboration_cannot into 'The opening balance is {level} from this file format' / 'Reader limit: {level}'). Also noted: apps/web/messages/ contains only en.json, so the AC's 'en and zh' half is vacuous today rather than skipped.
findings.required_fix: None required by the AC. Human copy for limit VALUES would be one follow-up covering every limit token, not a #782 fix.

findings.title: The registry version is not raised, and #782/#988 shipped as two migrations rather than the brief's shared cut
findings.evidence: Ticket lines: Sequencing — "The republish is shared with every other open ticket that republishes this registry in the same cut, #782 first among them ...: one migration, the version raised once across every touched row"; AC5 — "The registry version is raised exactly once for the whole republish, by updating existing rows, and every row published together carries the same value." Delivered as two migrations: 0245 (#782) raises 2 -> 3 over all 240 rows by UPDATE; 0246 (#988) raises nothing and moves zero rows. The lane's argument (report, 'Why the version does not move') is that a vocabulary widening republishes no content, with 0244 as the in-branch precedent, and that the wave-2 work-order addendum requires one migration per ticket at its reserved number, which forbids the shared cut. Verified: 0246's prestate and tail both assert count(distinct registry_version) = 1, min = 3, 240 rows, and the high-water mark in agreement; the re-run battery confirms PUBLISHED_REGISTRY_VERSION = 3 live. Net effect across the cut matches the AC's intent — the version rose exactly once, over every touched row.
findings.required_fix: None. Keep the reasoning visible in the release record so the hosted publish is not read as a missed raise.

findings.title: The new level's basis requirement, and the message-key manifest, are asserted by nothing
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "A pairing at the new level carries a `basis` stating what it proposes and why it stops short of posting." The honesty-invariant cell added to document-capability-registry.test.mjs checks only `business_operation = 'proposal_only' and typed_facts <> 'supported'`; nothing checks that such a row's basis says what it proposes. 0191's basis sentence is composed at seed time by a CASE with no proposal_only arm (0191:406-409), so a future proposal_only row would fall to 'The operation is an accepted target and is not built.' unless its own migration writes the sentence. Vacuous today — zero rows carry the level, which the same cell proves. Separately, capability-registry.test.ts:164 asserts TIER_STATE_KEYS contains 'capabilityTier.proposal_only' "so a completeness check over it would catch a missing translation", but no such completeness check exists: TIER_STATE_KEYS has no consumer outside its own test file. The en.json key was added by hand and is present (en.json:2677).
findings.required_fix: None blocking. When the first pairing is classified proposal_only, its migration must write the basis sentence and a cell must pin it; a messages-completeness cell over TIER_STATE_KEYS would make the manifest's stated purpose real.
